what: Step 0 of the game company design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-16-game-company-watch-and-commentary-design.md): what two models wrote about 4 frames of a game screen, how each note was judged against its frames, and the screen-change numbers of every rendered sequence. Words and numbers only. The frames, saves and ROMs are not in the repo.
how_judged: By eye against the frames, by the session that ran step 0. One judge, not blind. The operator saw the set and answered that it is good enough to build on.
how_rendered: Sequences are 60 s of scripted input from real saves, rendered in the Retro image with no browser, one frame kept every 2 s. A look gets 4 frames from the last 30 s of the sequence (at 30, 40, 50 and 60 s), oldest first, enlarged 2 or 3 times. walk_NN: walk in four directions in turn and swing the sword, from save NN. ctl_idle: no input (a Game Over menu). menu_x: open the item menu and move the cursor. map_x: press the map key. long_x_dir: hold one direction. <game>_still_N / <game>_walk_N: no input / the walk plan, on two NES games.

prompts.first: You are the eyes of Orion for a video game that someone else is playing. You describe. You do not judge, and you do not speak to anyone. Write one short note of at most 300 characters: where the player's character is, what they are doing, and what changed across the frames. Use only what is visible in the frames. Do not use a name for the player. If you cannot tell what is shown, write exactly: unclear. If nothing changed since your last note, write exactly: nothing new.
prompts.stateless: You are the eyes of Orion for a video game that someone else is playing. You describe. You do not judge, and you do not speak to anyone. Write one short note of at most 300 characters: where the player's character is, what they are doing, and what changed across the frames. Read any words shown on the screen exactly as written. Use only what is visible in the frames. Do not use a name for the player. If you cannot tell what is shown, write exactly: unclear.

sequences.frames_show: A still "GAME OVER" menu with three options. Nothing moves.

looks.note: nothing new
nothing new

The screen displays a "GAME OVER" menu with options to save and continue, save and quit, or continue without saving. A small character sprite stands next to the top option. The HUD shows 1.5 hearts remaining, a full green meter, and a bomb selected. Across the frames, the menu remains open with no selection made.
The screen displays "GAME OVER" with menu options. The player's character is not visible as the game has ended. No change occurred between the frames.

The screen shows a "GAME OVER" message with three options: "Save And Continue," "Save And Quit," and "Do Not Save And Continue." The player's character is not visible, as the game has ended. The inventory bar at the top remains unchanged, indicating no new items were collected. The hearts representing lives are also unchanged. No action is being taken by the player, as the game is paused at the game over screen.

The screen displays a black background with the text "GAME OVER" in purple. Below, a menu offers three options: "Save And Continue", "Save And Quit", and "Do Not Save And Continue". A small character sprite is positioned to the left of the first option. The top HUD shows 1/3 bombs, 372 rupees, 29 blue items, 40 arrows, 1 key, and an empty life meter. The scene is static across all frames.

wrong_details: 1/3 bombs (the mark is the magic meter's)

sequences.frames_show: A cave room. The map key was pressed and no map opened. The character stands still by a dark pit; nothing moves in the four frames.

looks.note: The character stands on a dirt path in a dark cave, facing right toward a small hole in the rock wall. The equipped item is a bomb. The character remains completely stationary across all four frames, with no change to the environment, health, or inventory.

verdict.remark: still scene described as still; the screen change of this window is 0.0000, so the trigger would have skipped it

sequences.frames_show: The world map, zoomed in on a mountain ledge under cloud. Markers blink: a number 7, a blue crystal, and the small head that marks the player's position. This is a map, not a play scene; nobody walks.

looks.note: The character is on a rocky ledge in a snowy area. A blue gem appears on a lower ledge to the right, and the character moves toward it. The character then disappears from the screen, leaving only the gem visible.

wrong_details: read as a play scene: a character walking on a snowy ledge toward a gem
verdict.remark: the world map was not recognised as a map

sequences.frames_show: The item menu, open. The name box reads MAGIC MIRROR, FIREROD, BOW & ARROWS, MAGIC POWDER in the four frames. The crystals panel shows six blue crystals and one grey one.
